Physician-examiners who take the Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE) are permitted to participate remotely, according to preliminary study findings. However, further validity evidence is required before this practice can be recommended for use in high-stakes examinations.

This means that physician-examiners may still need to complete the OSCE face-to-face or with a proctor in some instances. It's essential to note that this does not apply to all examinations, and specific details should be reviewed on a case-by-case basis.

To confirm whether remote participation is feasible for an examination, it's crucial to check with the institution or examiners directly, as well as review any relevant guidelines or policies.
